Five LLM agents cover problem framing, data work, analysis, critique, and writing. A state-machine coordinator supports revision loops, checkpoint recovery, and sandboxed code runs. From a prompt and dataset, it produces a full LaTeX paper with real citations and peer review. Current limits include single-dataset scope and formulaic output; causal and multi-dataset work is planned.
arxiv-2603-18373: Hong and Quan uncover visual sycophancy and split beliefs in vision-language models. Their tri-layer diagnostic splits perception, dependency, and alignment failures with three per-sample metrics. Across 9 models and 9,000 samples under blind, noise, and conflict tests, 72.9% show visual sycophancy. Internal evidence stays intact, yet a hallucinated answer is decoded; no sample showed robust refusal. Scaling cuts language shortcuts but amplifies the sycophancy pattern.
arxiv-2603-18873: Catalan and co-authors survey Duolingo users on work-related lessons. Five staff at a multinational firm in the Philippines shared their experience. General scenarios like greetings and food orders appear far more often than work ones. Users found the general lessons relatable and good for grammar, vocabulary, and culture. Work lessons, when present, add the domain words that build professional fluency. Each person asked for distinct scenarios, so one fixed set fits poorly. The authors propose adaptive lessons tailored to each learner.
arxiv-2603-19273: Faruna builds the first safety test for harmful prompts in low-resource West African languages. Models refuse most harmful asks in English, but those guards may fail in other tongues. The LSR test sends matched probes in English and in Yoruba, Hausa, Igbo, and Igala. A new drift score shows how much English refusal is lost in each tongue. On Gemini 2.5 Flash, refusal falls from about 90 percent to 35 to 55 percent. Igala shows the worst drop, with drift of 0.55.
arxiv-2603-19773: Braeutigam, Stock, and Egger detect objects from templates without any model training. Most detectors learn from data and need a training set. Their target uses have low variation but strict cost limits. One use is automatic testing of graphical interfaces. The method takes segments from a segmentation foundation model. A simple feature-based classifier then labels those segments. Tests targeted icons in navigation maps for car software testing. The results came close to trained detectors such as YOLO.
arxiv-2603-19973: Clerico studies whether dominating affine functionals can be picked in a Borel measurable way. Families of finite-dimensional functions may each admit some affine bound from above. Standard uniformisation theorems do not seem to settle if such bounds can be chosen measurably. Clerico proves a Borel selector does exist under semi-analytic regularity assumptions. The proof joins a one-dimensional insertion result, drawn from Lusin's separation theorem, with induction on dimension. As a use case, he gets Borel selections of subgradients for convex functions that depend on a parameter.
arxiv-2603-20373: Bailey and co-authors extend Bondi accretion theory to include radiative feedback. Classic Bondi flow ignores the heating and cooling of infalling gas. They build steady, spherical solutions with constant opacity in gas-pressure settings. Four dimensionless parameters control the solutions across a wide range. Feedback mainly works to suppress accretion, unlike in radiation-pressure settings. The effect grows strongest at high optical depth and luminosity. Analytic formulas confirm the suppression and its scaling laws. The results matter most for planet formation settings.
arxiv-2603-20573: Wei and co-authors present immUNITY, a defense against low volume and slow network attacks. Recent traces show up to 71 percent of flows look suspect. Yet each attack flow may hold just a few packets. Their design pairs a programmable switch with a SmartNIC. A lean filter sends benign traffic straight on. The SmartNIC checks the rest with learned classifiers and rules. Tests on Tofino and BlueField 3 hardware gave high accuracy.
arxiv-2603-20673: Huang and co-authors present PAVE, a check layer for retrieval augmented language models. Such models can grab good evidence yet answer before they test it. PAVE first breaks the retrieved text into small facts tied to the question. It drafts an answer and scores how well the facts back it. Weak drafts get revised before the final reply. In tests with fixed retrieval, PAVE beat simpler baselines. The top gain reached 32.7 accuracy points on one benchmark.
arxiv-2603-20973: Dutta and co-authors measure how real network structure changes as networks grow. They use a large corpus of networks from four scientific domains. They track mean degree, transitivity, mean geodesic distance, and degree assortativity against network size. All four domains show consistent scaling laws, though at different rates. They then test three random graph models against these laws. Configuration model graphs match the scaling well. Models with modular structure do slightly better. The laws give new targets for testing models of network structure.
arxiv-2603-21073: Chen and co-authors compose long-form music by first generating it at high speed. Long music is hard to model because long audio strains memory and compute. Their SqueezeComposer assumes models can work with sped up audio, at two, four, or eight times speed. A diffusion model generates in the sped up domain, then refines after the audio is slowed back down. They test long-form generation and whole song singing accompaniment. Results show the trick yields efficient, high quality long music.
arxiv-2603-21273: Jiang and co-authors study the atmospheres of five hot Jupiters near the edge of the Neptune desert. The sample holds two ultra-hot Jupiters, two classic hot Jupiters, and one hot Neptune. With high resolution spectroscopy, they search for absorption signals. Three denser planets show no significant absorption. WASP-117b gives marginal hydrogen and lithium signals. WASP-167b shows a strong iron signal by cross-correlation, and a retrieval yields metal abundances and a temperature near twenty five hundred kelvin.
arxiv-2603-21373: Batorski and Swoboda propose PLR, a probabilistic method to order in-context learning examples. Model performance depends heavily on example order, but searching all orderings is infeasible. PLR replaces the discrete search with a learned Plackett-Luce distribution over orderings. Its parameters shift toward orderings that score well on the task metric. On several classification benchmarks, PLR improves few-shot accuracy at all tested shot counts. It also helps on math reasoning tasks, where label based ordering methods do not apply.
arxiv-2603-21573: Tsaprazlis and co-authors argue that privacy risk in images is compositional, not binary. Harmless details can combine into a serious exposure, yet benchmarks mostly label images private or not. Their Compositional Privacy Risk Taxonomy sorts visual attributes by how identifying they are alone and in combination. It defines four severity levels plus a scoring function for continuous risk. They built a 6,700-image dataset aligned with the taxonomy. Frontier vision models matched the graded scores with guidance, but smaller models struggled.
arxiv-2603-22173: Mittal and co-authors report a two-dimensional realization of the parity anomaly. The anomaly appears when a classical symmetry cannot survive quantization. For one 2D Dirac fermion, it forces a half-quantized Hall response. Such effects were seen before only on 3D insulator surfaces. The team builds a synthetic 2D system from ultracold dysprosium atoms. One dimension is real space, the other encoded in spin states. At the transition point, the bulk gap closes at one Dirac point. There they observe a robust half-quantized Hall drift.
arxiv-2603-22273: Mhammedi and Cohan split exploration away from policy training in reinforcement learning. Standard agents mix the two, using policy machinery just to widen state coverage. The authors argue that this overhead is wasteful. Their method explores with tree search, guided by an uncertainty measure. No reinforcement learning runs during the search phase. They report about ten times wider coverage than intrinsic motivation baselines. The found paths can then be distilled into working policies. Those policies set strong scores on Montezuma's Revenge, Pitfall, and Venture.
arxiv-2603-22573: Vogels and co-authors present Multiple Jump MCMC, a faster way to sample over binary model spaces. Such spaces appear in graphical models, variable selection, mixtures, and trees. Classic samplers wander them slowly. Their method is simple, never rejects a move, and runs fast in practice. On Gaussian graphical models it beats the best rival by two orders of magnitude, handling half a million parameters in under a minute. Theorems in the work pin down how well it tracks the true posterior.
arxiv-2603-22673: Ma and co-authors compare what students and teachers want from AI coding assistants. Such tools give on-demand explanations and debugging help in programming courses. The team surveyed 50 educators and 90 students in parallel. They asked about how help should be sought, given, and controlled. Teachers favored indirect hints that protect student reasoning. Students preferred direct, practical help. Teachers also wanted course-aligned limits and oversight tools. Students stressed fast, clear support when stuck. The authors turn these gaps into design guidance for learning-focused assistants.
arxiv-2603-22873: Barchiesi, Henao, Mora-Corral, and Rodiac exhibit a Lavrentiev gap in the neo-Hookean model of elasticity. The setting is three-dimensional nonlinear elasticity. They construct boundary data with a striking split. The lowest energy over deformations with natural regularity and invertibility is strictly higher. That higher value exceeds the infimum over the weak closure of the same class. A deformation with a dipole-type singularity drives the gap. The result shows energy values can depend sharply on the function class allowed.
arxiv-2603-22973: Floro and co-authors study how to detect implicit legal citations in French court decisions. A court may apply a Civil Code rule without naming it. Their benchmark holds about one thousand passage-article pairs, labeled by three legal experts. Cases the experts dispute are where models fail, they find. Their best ensemble reaches a solid overall score. Two-thirds of its false positives land on disputed cases. Ranking with multi-model consensus lifts precision for top candidates. Expert disagreement itself flags task uncertainty, they argue.
arxiv-2603-23373: Yuan and six co-authors test the cosmic distance duality relation with lensed gravitational waves. The relation ties luminosity distance to angular diameter distance at each redshift. They simulate strongly lensed signals from massive binary black holes seen by space detectors. Ten events span source redshifts 2 to 6 under a point-mass lens model. A deviation parameter is folded straight into the waveform fit. Joining Taiji and LISA data roughly doubles the precision for one event. Across ten events, the bounds stay tight and match zero deviation.
arxiv-2603-23773: Shepherd tracks audience behavior across 18 linked streaming channels over 3.3 years. The data hold 2.9 million minute-level view counts from 7,762 livestreams. When more channels stream at once, raw viewers per stream fall sharply. Controls for time of day shrink much of that link, so scheduling explains a large share. Detected viewer transfer events move about half the audience at the median. Loyalty scores vary widely by creator, which suggests loyalty sits with creators, not the group.
arxiv-2603-23873: Agostinelli presents DeepXube, a free Python package for solving pathfinding problems with learned heuristics. The tool trains heuristic functions with deep reinforcement learning, then guides search with them. It includes Bellman-based learning, hindsight experience replay, and batched search methods such as weighted A* and beam search. Goals can be stated with answer-set programming. Training data generation runs in parallel across CPUs, and updates run across GPUs. The package also offers visualization, profiling, and progress monitoring through a command-line tool.
arxiv-2603-23973: Das and Manocha present SLAT-Phys, a fast method that predicts material properties of 3D objects from one image. Such fields matter for simulation, robotics, and digital twins. Their method skips explicit 3D reconstruction. It uses organized latent features from a pretrained 3D generation model, which encode shape and meaning. A light decoder then predicts Young's modulus, density, and Poisson's ratio at each point. It takes 9.9 seconds per object on one GPU. That is about 120 times faster than prior methods, they report.
arxiv-2603-24073: Kang and co-authors introduce concept-level deficiency prediction for knowledge tracing. Standard tracing predicts whether a student will answer right or wrong. It cannot say which concept the student is missing. Their ConceptKT dataset labels both the concepts each question needs and the concepts behind wrong answers. They test in-context learning with large language and reasoning models. Picking past records by conceptual alignment and semantic similarity works best. It improves both correctness prediction and concept-level diagnosis, they report.
arxiv-2603-24173: Karzhemanov studies surjective rational maps on smooth projective surfaces. He proves a couple of dynamical properties of such maps. He also gives a numerical condition that ensures the map is regular. Worked examples and calculations in the study relate to the topological entropy of the map. The results add basic structure facts for surface dynamics. His test gives a concrete check that can be applied to given examples.
arxiv-2603-24373: Cui and co-authors present PP-OCRv5, a text recognition system with only five million parameters. It rivals much larger vision-language models on standard OCR benchmarks, with sharper text location and fewer made-up words. The team traces this result to data, not scale. They measure how data difficulty, accuracy, and diversity each shape performance. Their tests show that a classic two-stage OCR pipeline can go far when fed enough clean, varied, well-labelled data.
arxiv-2603-24573: Dasu and Criger design flag circuits that catch errors in non-Clifford rotation gates. Their recursively defined circuits detect logical errors induced by faulty rotations on CSS codes with fault distance two. From these, they build circuits with cost linear in the precision level that implement fault-tolerant rotations on iceberg codes. They also give small circuits that prepare resource states in the Steane code for use in gate teleportation. The scheme extends to rotations with binary-digit angles, useful when time is digitised in simulations.
arxiv-2603-24673: Reich and co-authors report systematic Chandra monitoring of extreme X-ray variability in weak-line quasars. Ten quasars with weak C IV emission lines each gained three new Chandra observations, greatly improving coverage. One historically variable quasar rose in X-ray flux by a factor of at least six between 2023 and 2024. Another, once X-ray weak, varied by a factor of at least fourteen between 2019 and 2023. The fraction showing extreme variability is about 0.20. This favours wind motion over disk height changes as the driver.
arxiv-2603-24973: Fang and co-authors build BEACOF, a framework that helps language model agents work as a social group. Most such groups use fixed links, which can cause groupthink or deadlock. BEACOF treats each exchange as a game with hidden facts. Agents keep updating beliefs about what peers can do. They then shift between working together and arguing back, as the task needs. Tests in court, social, and medical scenes show fewer breakdowns and steadier paths to good answers.
arxiv-2603-25173: Liu and co-authors design a quantum battery that charges through a one-way magnetic link. Quantum batteries promise fast charging and dense storage, but noise drains them. Their setup uses two garnet spheres, one charger and one battery, joined by a waveguide. Chiral coupling lets energy flow one way and sets up a helpful interference. The battery stores 34 times more energy than a plain version, and yields 55 times more usable work. The link also allows remote-style charging and turns field noise into an asset.
arxiv-2603-25273: Zhang and Wiklicky add two new abstract domains to their probabilistic reading of neural networks. The framework tracks how input density flows through a net, and its grid domain chops space into boxes. One new domain fits smooth distributions to that flow. The other groups inputs into clusters. The pair explains how each domain works in theory. They give the matching abstract transformers and walk through small examples with pictures. The options widen the trade-offs between precision and cost in network analysis.
arxiv-2603-25573: Ahmed and co-authors teach species naming models to respect the tree of life. Field ID mixes specimen photos and DNA barcodes, but flat label training ignores how order, family, and genus nest. One variant shapes the embedding space level by level, so near kin stay near. A second adds a light fusion head that works with photo, DNA, or both. Across large biodiversity sets, accuracy beats strong rivals by over fourteen points. Gains grow when the DNA input is partial or corrupted.
arxiv-2603-25673: Jimenez-Oviedo and co-authors track how young children develop motor and thinking skills through tablet tasks. Their data covers children from 18 months to 8 years, across several school years. Six tasks test skills like fine motor control and reaction time. Clustering the results yields three groups: low, medium, and high performance. The authors report that the low group is highly stable in the early years. Over ninety percent of its members stay there. They argue such profiles could support early screening and tailored help.
arxiv-2603-25773: Zietsman argues that AI code review fails when no executable specification exists. Without an outside reference, the writing agent and the reviewing agent reason from the same code. They share training data and tend to fail in the same places. Zietsman sets out three hypotheses. Correlated errors in similar pipelines echo rather than cancel. Executable specs move a task from complex to merely complicated. The flaws specs cannot reach form a bounded residue fit for AI review. His order is specs first, checks second, AI review last.
arxiv-2603-26373: Jäger and Semin probe how hadron colliders can constrain axion-like particles through diboson production. They work in a linear effective field theory with bosonic couplings for these light, hypothetical particles. The study weighs the main production paths and backgrounds, with care for how often jets get misread. Using cautious misidentification rates, they derive joint bounds on couplings to gluons, weak bosons, and photons. They highlight what the high-luminosity LHC phase could reveal for masses below one GeV.
arxiv-2603-26473: Torres-Boy and co-authors steer the isomer mix of ions held inside superfluid helium droplets. They use a dual-oscillator infrared free-electron laser whose two colours can be tuned apart yet kept in tight sync. Their test ion is a singly deuterated proton-bound pair of dihydrogen phosphate and formate. Shining both colours on the droplets shifts which isomer form dominates. The setup also reveals infrared spectra of single isomers that stay hidden in one-colour runs.
arxiv-2603-26873: Aggarwal and Schoenrich remodel how the first stars' descendants got their chemical patterns. Very metal-poor stars are often assumed to carry the yield of one massive star. Odd abundance ratios in some stars were blamed on rare, very energetic hypernovae. The authors refit three such stars with a normal supernova instead. Uneven spread of the ejecta explains the patterns better than extreme energy. They argue all peculiar metal-poor stars need this reassessment.
arxiv-2603-26973: Legred and Yunes explain why stellar sequences reach a maximum mass and turn over. They recast the stellar structure equations as a dynamical system. In the relativistic regime, a fixed point appears in the Tolman-Oppenheimer-Volkoff equations. That fixed point lines up with the turnover of the mass-radius curve. It also lowers the effective dimension near instability, explaining equation-of-state-insensitive relations. A separate compressible limit governs weakly relativistic stars. Applying current constraints, they argue the pulsar J0740+6620 likely sits below the maximum mass.
arxiv-2603-27273: Elgouhary and El-Wakeel fuse global and local driving commands in a ROS2 arbitration module. A Pure Pursuit controller tracks the global reference path. A LiDAR-based gap follower reacts to nearby obstacles for safety. Neither controller is modified in their design. A PPO-trained policy predicts a continuous gate that blends both commands each step. Practical safety checks wrap the fused output. The team stresses the module with injected LiDAR noise, delay, and dropout. Safe success rates and controller runtime are reported as stress grows.
arxiv-2603-27473: Gu and co-authors hunt a subtle background in heavy-ion collisions. The chiral magnetic effect may signal CP violation in hot matter. Many past signals may stem from flow effects instead. This study sizes a fresh source: photon-nuclear reactions. Strong fields in each crash drive these reactions. Photon spin aligns with the field along the impact line. That setup can fake charge-based signals. The team estimates how large this fake share may be.
arxiv-2603-27573: Li and co-authors generate indoor 3D scenes that respect physics. SPREAD uses diffusion guided by a graph transformer. It learns space links and physical links jointly. Posed point clouds give the model geometric grounding. Built-in guides prevent collisions and respect gravity. Relation rules also shape each layout. Tests on 3D-FRONT and ProcTHOR lead the field. Scenes stay stable in physics simulation runs. The output suits embodied AI training worlds.
arxiv-2603-27773: Gao and co-authors match 3D shapes without regard to rotation. RINO learns dense correspondences in an unsupervised way. RINONet pulls features straight from raw geometry. Vector-based invariant learning handles the rotation side. Orientation-aware functional maps handle the rest. No pre-alignment or handcrafted descriptors are needed. Tests span bent, partial, noisy, and non-manifold shapes. Scores set new highs on hard matching tasks.
arxiv-2603-28773: Georgiev and co-authors introduce UltRAG, a simple recipe for retrieval-augmented generation over knowledge graphs. Language models often state false facts with confidence, and graph questions can need multi-hop reasoning. UltRAG joins three parts without any retraining. A language model generates queries, a fully inductive neural executor runs them, and a language model arbitrates the results. The system reached state-of-the-art results on knowledge graph question answering tasks. Ablation tests show that gains come from the full design, not one part alone.
arxiv-2603-28973: Polson, Sokolov, and Zantedeschi unify Bell inequalities, causal bounds, and quantum Bayesian computation in one framework. Bell inequalities mark the edge of classical hidden variable models, while quantum mechanics reaches the Tsirelson bound. They show the same polytope structure appears in causal inference. Instrumental inequalities and Balke-Pearl bounds are facets of the same polytope. Fine's theorem is the pivot that links the two fields. They extend the link to entropic forms, the NPA hierarchy, and undecidability results. A dictionary between the three fields follows.
arxiv-2603-29073: Zabolotskii studies specialization of cluster variables beyond the Laurent phenomenon. In a cluster algebra, a subset of initial cluster variables can be assigned values in a set way. After that step, all elements of the resulting algebra become polynomial in the remaining variables. That property allows every tame integral frieze pattern of type A to be obtained this way. The step includes the case where variables are set to zero. The short note states this route to frieze patterns in full. It rests on the polynomial behavior of that algebra.
arxiv-2603-29573: Lynch and co-authors show that stochastic and non-deterministic systems theories have clock systems. In categorical systems theory, behaviors are captured by maps into a system. Clock systems are handy because their behavior functors behave well by default. Whether such clocks exist for these two theory types was unknown. The authors prove that they do exist. For non-deterministic systems, the clocks point to wider notions of behavior. Those notions allow non-linear time. The work settles an open question in the area.
arxiv-2604-00073: Bechard and seven colleagues argue that enterprise automation does not need elaborate tool-based or web-browsing agents. A coding agent with only a terminal and a filesystem can do the job, working directly through platform programming interfaces. Across varied real systems, such stripped-down agents match or beat more complex designs. The authors conclude that simple programmatic interfaces paired with strong foundation models should anchor enterprise automation, at far lower cost and operational overhead.
arxiv-2604-00773: Mihael Arcan compares optimization strategies for mental-health text classification. He moves from classical and encoder baselines through LoRA and QLoRA fine-tuning to preference methods DPO, ORPO, and KTO. Results vary sharply by method: some approaches give stable, transferable gains, while others prove sensitive to settings and class balance. Method choice matters more than merely adding a preference stage, so he recommends preference optimization only where its gains are demonstrable.
arxiv-2604-00873: Tsutomu T. Takeuchi builds a geometric theory of cosmological peak counts from optimal transport and entropy geometry. He treats the density field as a Wasserstein-space probability measure and calls peaks still points with positive curvature. Their count becomes a curvature-conditioned measure. In the Gaussian-linear limit, this gives exactly the classic BBKS formula, and the theory also covers nonlinear change and early non-Gaussianity.
arxiv-2604-01373: Ye and Tang estimate the dissipativity of nonlinear systems from data, useful when no accurate model exists. From a Koopman operator model on a reproducing kernel Hilbert space, the storage function and supply rate become kernel quadratic forms. That turns the dissipative inequality into a linear operator inequality. Their linear-radial kernel encodes the equilibrium point. Functions in the space are locally at least linear near the origin, and kernel forms locally quadratic. From sampled-data kernel matrices, estimation becomes a convex optimization problem. A learning bound covers approximate correctness.
arxiv-2604-01473: Zhang and colleagues propose SelfGrader, a lightweight guardrail formulating jailbreak detection as grading using token-level logits. It evaluates safety within tokens, such as 0 to 9, and interprets their logit distribution as a safety signal. To align these signals with the safety rubric, it constructs PAC-guided anchor examples. It introduces a scoring rule considering harm and safety, yielding a score for harmfulness while reducing false alarms. Experiments across jailbreak benchmarks, adaptive attacks, benign benchmarks, language models, and baselines demonstrate robustness with low false alarm rates and latency.
arxiv-2604-01973: Cvejic and colleagues isolate identity from background context, which encoders tangle, using NearID distractors. NearID places twin cases on the same background as a reference image, removing shortcuts so identity discriminates. The team shares the NearID dataset, 19K identities with 316K matched distractors, plus a test protocol. Under that test, pretrained encoders score as low as 30.7 percent on SSR and rank distractors above matches. Identity-aware training on a backbone with a contrastive objective lifts that rate to 99.2 percent, improves scores by 28.0 percent, and aligns with judgments on DreamBench++.
arxiv-2604-02073: He and colleagues replace reasoning with latent reasoning for multimodal embedding. Explicit rationales help models infer intent, but they cost time and squeeze evidence into a narrow bottleneck. PLUME swaps reasoning for a latent rollout, steered by an adapter under the same budget. An explicit to latent curriculum stabilizes training with verbalized reasoning as a scaffold. On the 78-task MMEB benchmark, PLUME beats rivals, cutting it from hundreds of tokens to under 10 steps, over 30 times faster.
arxiv-2604-02873: Apadula, Grinbaum and Brukner study frame perspectives for quantum processes in the process-matrix formalism. For pure processes, causal reference frames and time-delocalized subsystems act as coordinate parametrizations of one perspective-neutral higher-order object. A genuine perspective needs extra frame data from an operational foliation into circuit fragments. They build unitary maps that switch perspectives for the quantum switch at the price of reshuffling past and future.
arxiv-2604-02973: Gu, Wang and Wang revisit text-to-motion generation through the lens of motion-language alignment. Their MLA-Gen framework joins broad motion priors, patterns learned from many motions, with fine-grained local conditioning tying each text detail to movement. The team also names an attention sink effect, where attention piles onto the first text token and starves later cues. A new SinkRatio metric measures that pile-up, and alignment-aware masking and control strategies ease it. Tests show better motion quality and alignment than strong baselines.
arxiv-2604-03073: Montanari and Doretti examine why Italy's department performance index, the ISPD, tends to polarize rankings. They trace part of the effect to scores clustering within departments, model that clustering as a function of department size, and build a fairer adjusted index. Fitted to rounded public data with a new Betoidal distribution, the adjusted index beat both the original and more data-hungry rivals in simulations.
arxiv-2604-03173: Rao, Wong, and Callison-Burch measure how often language models and research agents invent citation addresses that never existed. Across two large collections, they find 3 to 13 percent of citations are hallucinated and up to 18 percent fail to resolve, with research agents hallucinating more than search-aided models. Their open tool, urlhealth, checks links against the Wayback Machine and cuts unresolved citations below 1 percent in self-correction tests.
arxiv-2604-03573: Oyama and colleagues show with atom models that the heat and system-size link of dynamical heterogeneity in supercooled liquids fits a zero-temperature avalanche criticality picture. In these liquids, mid-size mobile and stuck domains grow upon cooling and show system-size dependence. Their work explains that dependence within the avalanche criticality picture.
arxiv-2604-03673: Greta Gorzoni and colleagues probed BERT-style models for knowledge of an Italian noun-preposition-noun pattern, the repeated-noun form seen in phrases like layer upon layer. They fed contextual word vectors into layer-by-layer classifiers to see where form and meaning of the construction live inside the model. The findings feed a wider debate between construction grammar and neural language modeling about what such models encode.
arxiv-2604-03773: Xingyu Miao and colleagues built M2StyleGS, a real-time 3D style transfer method that takes text or images as style guides instead of one fixed reference picture. It renders scenes with 3D Gaussian splatting, aligns CLIP text-visual features to VGG style features, and adds losses that hold color and style steady. Tests showed better visual quality and consistency gains of about 33 percent over prior work.
arxiv-2604-04273: Unlu introduces a search operator inspired by chromatin loop extrusion, the genome-folding process driven by motor complexes and barriers. The Loop-Extrusion Linkage wrapper learns which variables interact, orders them spectrally, and searches overlapping intervals grown by learned boundary odds. On six synthetic test functions, the full method wins the best median result on three at ten thousand evaluations, but simpler variants often beat it at fifty thousand. The strongest finding is that learned spectral ordering beats graph-only grouping and random ordering.
arxiv-2604-04673: Coulson and Wells examine Bayesian neural networks through statistical decision theory, where their optimality has drawn little attention. They study decision rules from deep, fully connected feedforward ReLU networks in the normal location model under quadratic loss. For fixed prior scales, they show the induced Bayes rule is not minimax. They then propose a hyperprior on the effective output variance that yields a superharmonic square-root marginal density. The resulting rule is both admissible and minimax, and the results extend to predictive density estimation under Kullback-Leibler loss.
arxiv-2604-05173: Karan and Majhi report a real origin of slack strings, got by framing string motion in finite-life settings. Leaving eternal strings, they construct a steady worldsheet kept to a finite region of Minkowski space-time, known as a causal diamond. The shrinking limit of the diamond worldsheet gives the birth setup, showing that slack strings arise only at the moment of birth. The new slack string phase is marked by a global Carrollian structure.
arxiv-2604-05273: Ahuja, Li, and Lampinen study whether language models can use subtext, meaning beyond literal content, introducing four suites. Settings range from allegories to games inspired by Dixit. Models bias toward overly literal communication, failing nuanced constraints; even the best generate literal clues 60 percent of times in Visual Allusions. Some models use common ground for subtext, cutting overly literal clues by 30 to 50 percent, but struggle to infer it when unstated. Paratextual and persona conditions shift allegory interpretation. The work quantifies subtext and reveals weaknesses of current models.
arxiv-2604-05873: Su, Tian, and Song improve multimodal sentiment analysis with PRISM, which keeps feeling clues in a set form instead of squashing them early. Clues sit in a shared prototype space so text, image, and sound can be compared, and live weights tune each mode's say as reasoning goes on. On three tests it beats strong rivals.
arxiv-2604-06373: Kashif and six colleagues test Cursor, an AI coding tool, on large-scale software builds using a Feature-Driven Human-In-The-Loop plan. They build 10 projects across three domains, guided by curated briefs. Manual checks give 91 percent average correctness, with projects at 16,965 lines across 114 files. CodeScene finds 1,305 issues in 9 categories; SonarQube finds 3,193 in 11 categories. Top issues are duplication, complexity, large methods, framework violations, exception handling, and accessibility. These violate SRP, SoC, and DRY principles, posing maintainability risks that demand review by experienced developers.
arxiv-2604-06673: Hwang and nine colleagues build a compact, electrically tuned mid-infrared source on a chip. Their optical parametric oscillator, integrated on thin-film lithium niobate, turns a fixed near-infrared pump laser into broadly tunable mid-infrared light. It produces 22 THz of multi-milliwatt radiation in a band prized for environmental, chemical, and biological sensing. Using the Vernier effect, the device tunes coarsely across multi-THz steps and smoothly within sub-100-GHz ranges without mode hops, opening a path to compact tunable sources.
arxiv-2604-06873: Yang and Yoshida generate local shields for decentralized partially observable agents. Safety fails when each agent's local action cannot fix the joint action, and existing shields assume a shared global state or use memoryless filters. Their shield process algebra, with guarded choice and recursion, specifies safe global behavior without communication. Compiling through an automaton to global and then local Mealy machines yields per-agent safe action sets from belief-style state subsets. A Rust implementation with PRISM safety probabilities cuts collisions sharply in a path-finding case study.
arxiv-2604-07173: Chen and eight colleagues present InfiniLoRA, a serving design that separates small task adapters from the main language model during inference. A shared adapter server schedules work with an eye to latency targets and uses fast links plus specialized kernels to keep the extra step cheap. In their tests the split design serves about three times as many requests under strict latency limits and lifts the share of adapters meeting those limits.
arxiv-2604-07373: KR and Samanta study clusters of co-rotating vortices in compact fluid domains, which spin as a whole while slowly breathing in size. They model a doubly periodic inviscid domain with an exact Schottky-Klein prime-function representation. The two-vortex case reduces to one complex degree of freedom, yielding explicit rotation and translation formulas. A small-cluster expansion then splits the motion into planar interactions, torus corrections, and geometry-driven anisotropic modes, all encoded at leading order in one complex quadrupole moment confirmed by simulation.
arxiv-2604-07773: Li writes a practical guide to reading public opinion and behavior through social media and review platforms as a kind of distributed, human-centered sensing. The workflow runs from platform-aware collection through information extraction and geographic anchoring to statistical modeling, with language models helping to pull structure from noisy posts. Four case studies show the approach at work: vaccine acceptance, earthquake damage, airport service quality, and accessibility in city environments.
arxiv-2604-07973: Zhao and ten colleagues benchmark large multimodal models on goal-oriented navigation in urban 3D spaces to test spatial action. Such models show strong visual-linguistic reasoning, but spatial decision capacity stays unclear. The team spent over 500 hours building a dataset of 5,037 high-quality navigation samples emphasizing vertical actions and rich urban semantics. They then assess 17 representative models spanning non-reasoning models, reasoning models, agent-based methods, and vision-language-action models. Current models show emerging action skills yet remain far from human-level performance.
arxiv-2604-08273: Sil and seven colleagues study CH+ excitation in the planetary nebula NGC 7027. Small carbon hydride cations like methylidyne CH+ matter in deep-space chemistry. They join gas-phase reaction networks forming hydrocarbons, precursors to complex organic matter. CH+ is a highly reactive ion rapidly destroyed by H, H2, and electrons, making its states hard to model. Its level counts depend on radiative and inelastic processes plus formation and destruction rates, called chemical pumping. The team studies this effect with new ab initio collision data.
arxiv-2604-08573: Todescato and Carbonera introduce Soft Silhouette Loss, a differentiable objective that teaches deep representations global cluster structure. Each sample is scored against every class in its batch, pushing it nearer its own class than rivals, unlike pairwise losses that see only pairs or proxies. Combined with cross entropy and contrastive learning, the hybrid tops baselines on seven datasets, lifting average top accuracy to 39.08 percent.
arxiv-2604-08673: Woolley studies mixed four point correlators of half BPS operators in theories with eight real supercharges, in 3D through 6D. Using a known basis of solutions to the superconformal Ward identity, he shows dynamical data at extremality two lives in simpler reduced correlator functions with block expansions. The reduced blocks use ordinary blocks with shifted kinematics, reproducing known four and six dimensional cases and giving new results in 3D and 5D.
arxiv-2604-08773: Bresciani and Yang study neutral representations: a representation V of a group G is neutral when every twisted form over a field has a point. Twisted forms arise from variety families, quotient singular points, and Tannaka classes as bundles on gerbes, giving many uses for fields of moduli. The paper sorts neutral faithful representations of finite groups up to size three. It gives an easy neutral test for finite abelian groups in any size. It builds a normal form for gerbe morphisms, showing it depends only on shape type.
arxiv-2604-09073: Wen and three colleagues exploit the fault tolerance of diffusion models to cut energy and latency. Dynamic voltage and frequency scaling offers accelerator gains, but past methods either gain little or degrade output quality. Their DRIFT method pairs a rollback safety net, which fixes only critical errors by going back to earlier steps, with offload gaps and reorganized layouts. Tests across varied models and data sets show energy cut by over a third through low voltage, or runs sped 1.7 times via fast clocks, with quality kept.
arxiv-2604-09273: Tammen and colleagues use light scattering to study Pluronic triblock copolymers, whose high-temperature behavior resists old flow tests. From scattered light signals they extract thickness and find where micelles form and at what level for F127 solutions from 5 to 80 degrees Celsius. The high EO/PO ratio and varied chain lengths of F127 prove critical to its high-temperature re-entrant liquid phase, as PEO solubility falls and the PPO core dries out. Elastic measures help pin down phase shifts and reveal solid-phase mechanics that usual tracking cannot reach.
arxiv-2604-09373: Migliorini and colleagues examine real traits of dextran mixes as model crowding media for living systems. Man-made crowders used to model large-molecule crowding in vitro are often poorly described. The authors examine density, thickness, and flow in crowded dextran systems, finding size-linked trends tied to overlap strength with a Flory power of about four tenths. Thickness rises as a power law, self-motion decays fast, water spread falls regardless of size, and results yield the true crowder volume fraction counting for bound water.
arxiv-2604-09573: Röber and four colleagues test which kinds of post-hoc explanations actually help users grasp and trust black-box models. In an online study, people faced four arms: no explanation, feature importance scores, point counterfactuals, and interval counterfactuals. Interval explanations clearly beat the rest at raising both model understanding and shown trust. Point counterfactuals, by contrast, showed no supported gain over the control group. Traits such as cognitive style shaped how well each explanation worked.
arxiv-2604-09773: Chattopadhyay and four co-authors model 47 Tuc's most massive black hole from cluster evolution and binary dynamics. They evolve 80,000 realizations in baseline and extended scenarios. Matching 47 Tuc's mass and half-mass radius, hierarchical mergers alone yield a retained black hole of about 45 to 70 solar masses with spin about 0.65, limited to about 1 to 3 mergers. In the extended scenario, most seeds are ejected, but about 10 percent above 450 solar masses survive, yielding 90th-percentile retained masses of about 500 to 1,100 solar masses. The results favour a remnant subsystem over a single massive black hole.
arxiv-2604-09873: Schonfeld and nine co-authors present a sturdier non-contact platform for high-temperature conductivity, built on differential radiometry. Contact methods falter from contact resistance, uncertain boundaries, and radiative losses, blocking data for hypersonic and fusion parts. The method pairs lock-in infrared imaging with a modulated laser spot, plus pyrometry and a heat model. Using pure molybdenum, they report conductivity from 1,500 to 3,000 Kelvin, near melting, with uncertainties of about 8 to 11 percent, plus emittance data. The work closes a high-temperature data gap and adds melt-adjacent radiative data.
arxiv-2604-10373: Emmanouilidis, Vlatakis-Gkaragkounis, and Vidal sharpen fixed step stochastic methods for min-max tasks. Many learning tasks, from robust training to multi agent play, fit min-max or variational inequality frames. Shuffling data cuts mean squared error, while Richardson Romberg averaging cuts bias a second time. Joined, the pair wins on both fronts, adding a cubic bias cut in structured non monotone cases. Large trials back the theory, showing steady speed gains across test tasks in practice.
arxiv-2604-10673: Razeghi argues that AI alignment cannot rest on stated principles alone, because principles rarely settle their own application in concrete cases. When principles clash, run too broad, or meet unclear facts, judgment must step in. Alignment therefore includes an interpretive component: context-sensitive readings of how principles should be applied and ranked. Evidence from preference-labeling data shows many cases fall into conflict or indifference, where no principle uniquely decides. Since such judgments surface in behavior, deployment-time responses matter more than off-policy audits alone can capture.
arxiv-2604-10873: Choi offers a working, numeric definition of intelligence for physical systems. Intelligence density is the log of independent outputs over description length: a system memorizes if description grows with outputs, and knows if it stays fixed while outputs diverge. Knowing is generalization: a finite device giving right outputs across endless inputs, not stored ones. Meaning is a pick and order of functions giving outputs where rightness can be stated; contextuality is one over conditional Kolmogorov complexity. These refute Searle's premise, that syntax falls short of semantics, where rightness is statable.
arxiv-2604-11373: Shangguan, Di Nuovo, and Cangelosi show that minimal embodiment helps a robot learn number concepts from sensorimotor experience. A neural model counting through interaction with a Franka Panda arm reaches 96.8 percent counting accuracy with only 10 percent of training data, against 60.6 percent for vision-only baselines, and the edge survives randomized visual-motor pairings. The model develops number-selective units with logarithmic tuning, a mental number line, Weber-law scaling, and rotational dynamics tied to magnitude, mirroring children's path from subset-knowers to cardinal-principle knowers.
arxiv-2604-11573: Artiano, Ranocha, and Samantaray design higher-order implicit IMEX Runge-Kutta schemes for the anelastic limit of isentropic Euler equations under gravity. In the zero-Mach-number limit, compressible Euler flows settle into a varied-density anelastic incompressible system. Their schemes preserve asymptotics and balance, combining penalization of a linear steady state, balance-preserving finite-volume reconstruction, and steady-state-preserving source grids. The penalization keeps the scheme implicit, and well-balanced flux-source grids hold accuracy at very low Mach numbers. Case studies back the theory.
arxiv-2604-11873: Cronin and forty-one colleagues image the inner five kiloparsecs of the M82 superwind with JWST, tracing polycyclic aromatic hydrocarbons in a network of cool wind filaments. PAH brightness falls with the inverse square of distance from the midplane out to 2.5 kiloparsecs, driven by the starburst radiation field, while band ratios shift only modestly toward larger grains. PAH abundance sits near 1 percent in the starburst and stays flat out to 5 kiloparsecs, suggesting grains sheltered in cool cloud surfaces survive at least about 20 million years.
arxiv-2604-12373: Ashuach and four colleagues ask whether language models hold privileged knowledge of their own answer correctness, beyond what external observation reveals. Correctness classifiers trained on a model's own hidden states show no advantage over peer-model probes under standard evaluation. The authors trace this null result to high inter-model agreement. On disagreement subsets where models conflict, self-representations win for factual knowledge tasks but not for math reasoning, with the factual edge emerging progressively from early-to-mid layers onward.
arxiv-2604-12473: Christopher D. Wallbridge and Erwin Jose Lopez Pulgarin argue robots should recover from errors, not just avoid them. Many AI systems chase single-shot performance beyond human baselines. Real work is continuous and interactive, where mistakes are inevitable. Humans succeed partly by catching and learning from errors. The position paper asks how robotic systems can detect and recover from their own mistakes. Robotic nuclear gloveboxes illustrate the challenge concretely. Simple starting designs point a way forward.
arxiv-2604-12973: Jonathan Coles and 22 colleagues recount training the open Apertus model on the Alps supercomputer. Sovereign AI drives governments to seek local data-compliant models. Training at 70 billion parameters on GH200 chips marks a first for academia. Storage bottlenecks and unstable interconnects tested the team. Lessons turn the supercomputer into a resilient software-defined learning platform. Post-training needs and platform growth beyond one run close the account.
arxiv-2604-13073: Yan and six colleagues build OmniTrace, a framework that traces each generated sentence back to the text chunks, images, or seconds of audio and video it came from. It reads late-layer attention during the single generation pass, needing no extra runs and no per-modality tuning. In one pass it recovers 77 to 96 percent of the effect of leave-one-out attribution, which needs up to 41 extra passes. Its rankings match human-marked evidence better than the strongest baseline.
arxiv-2604-13273: Baikalov, Bagautdinov, and Muravyov tackle semantic ID staleness in generative search, where usage-based identifiers drift from recent user behavior. Prior work either freezes the ID vocabulary or rebuilds it entirely with retraining, but time drift is rarely studied. Their lightweight model-free matching update maps new identifiers onto the existing set, keeping the checkpoint usable for warm-start tuning. Across three tests it lifts recall and ranking at high ranks over naive tuning with stale IDs. It cuts training compute by about 8 to 9 times over full rebuilds.
arxiv-2604-13473: Davidson, Lera, and Mahari examine what drives rise from United States District Courts to Courts of Appeals. They use a panel with over 36,000 cases since 1930, with a discrete-time hazard model tracking yearly rise odds. Rises show a life-cycle pattern, strongly shaped by political match between judges and leaders. Elite degrees and output raise rise chances, while more losses on appeal lower them. Citation links also matter apart from elite degrees. In short, timing, politics, networks, and work shape who rises, with politics on top.
arxiv-2604-13573: Chen and five colleagues replace one-way transfer between markets with joint work in cross-market sequential recommendation. Their federated framework, FeCoSR, pretrains all markets together on shared behavior patterns. It then fine-tunes locally for market-specific tastes, so no source market sacrifices itself for others. A semantic soft cross-entropy loss tempers the market differences that otherwise degrade joint training. Experiments on real datasets show clear gains over prior methods.
arxiv-2604-13773: Francis and 22 colleagues survey hydrogen winds and jets from low-mass protostars with JWST's MIRI. They observe 13 single and 20 multiple protostars in Class 0 and I, mapping hydrogen and ALMA carbon monoxide data. Low-energy transitions trace wide, slow winds; high-energy ones mark shocks and knots. Wind opening angles widen from about 20 degrees to about 90 degrees from Class 0 to Class I. Warm gas at 600 kelvin carries a hundred times the hot mass. Mass-loss rates fall a hundredfold from Class 0 to II, tracking luminosity. That matches disk wind models.
arxiv-2604-14173: Pasicki proves a criterion for Cauchy sequences in db-metric spaces. It refines an earlier criterion from a 2025 paper on Cauchy sequences in b-metric spaces. The note sharpens the prior criterion rather than starting from scratch, with the new test turning on whether sequence terms draw ever closer together.
arxiv-2604-14273: Sultan and three colleagues study accretion and spin in the circumgalactic medium with FIRE simulations. Halos near a trillion solar masses mark transitions to virialized inner media, steady star formation, and thin disks. Inflows run almost entirely cold before virialization, while hot inflows rule after, cooling as they circularize at galaxy radii. Cold inflows carry more spin than dark matter and hot gas. In bursty low-mass galaxies they form stars before circularizing, while in steady galaxies hot inflows circularize and cool before forming stars with disk-like motion.
arxiv-2604-14373: Wu, Cao, Li, and Gong build SatBLIP, a satellite vision-language system that reads rural landscapes to predict county-level social vulnerability. Structured tile notes on roofs, yards, greenery, and roads, first drafted with GPT-4o, train a satellite-tuned BLIP model to caption new images. Captions plus language-model embeddings feed a vulnerability estimate, and SHAP attribution flags roof form and condition, street width, vegetation, and open space as steady drivers. The setup maps rural risk settings in an interpretable way.
arxiv-2604-14673: Cai, Lin, and Zhou settle a spectral extremal problem for signed bipartite graphs. In such a graph each edge carries a plus or minus sign, and the graph is unbalanced when some cycle holds an odd count of negative edges. Among unbalanced signed bipartite graphs with no negative four-cycle, they identify the unique graphs attaining the largest spectral radius, up to switching isomorphism. The result holds both for fixed part sizes and for fixed total order, extending a recent uniqueness theorem into a Turán-style setting.
arxiv-2604-14773: Su, Liu, Hu, Lu, Xia, and Liu built CoPA, a test for judging how well question-answering systems tailor their answers to each user. It mines cases where individual choices override community consensus, boiling six user factors down into scoring dimensions. The test holds 1,985 user profiles for fine-grained, factor-level assessment. By scoring fit with cognitive preferences inferred from interaction patterns, CoPA tells systems apart more sharply than generic similarity scores. Code is public.
arxiv-2604-14873: Seaton, Speake, and Todorov develop highly coarse-grained polarisable water models for mesoscopic simulations. Soft-matter thermodynamics and transport hinge on representation, and polar solvents like water need dielectric effects captured through charge distributions and network structuring. Coarse-grained dynamics and dissipative particle dynamics still leave such dielectric effects open. The authors polarise their earlier non-polar nDPD water model for liquid electrolytes and solvated organic membranes. They test its fitness as a dielectric medium against TIP3P, while tracking changes to properties the non-polar model already handled well.
arxiv-2604-15073: Rahman and colleagues survey security checking for system-on-chip designs through hardware emulation. Simulation and formal proof often miss flaws that appear only under long, realistic, hostile runs, they note. Emulation runs chip designs faster under lifelike hardware and software loads while keeping enough detail for security study. The survey maps past work and weighs where emulation adds most, framing it as a growing pre-silicon tool.
arxiv-2604-15173: Helvaci and Cheung target the costliest part of time-based action segmentation: labeling action boundaries in untrimmed video. Their B-ACT framework spends a fixed clip budget where errors cluster, ranking videos by prediction uncertainty and then picking top boundaries by a new score. That score blends nearby uncertainty, class mix-ups, and time-based prediction shifts to rank each frame's importance. The two-stage loop aims to buy the most accuracy per labeled clip.
arxiv-2604-15273: Innan and three colleagues run a fair head-to-head test of how node embeddings, the numeric summaries fed to graph neural networks, affect graph classification. Classical methods and quantum-oriented variants share one backbone, splits, and training budget across five TU sets and a converted QM9 set. Quantum-oriented embeddings win most steadily on structure-led sets, while plain social graphs still suit classical methods.
arxiv-2604-15373: Murphy proposes InfoChess, a two-player game that makes information gathering itself the contest, with no piece captures to muddy the stakes. Pieces serve only to change what each side can see, and players score on how well they infer the enemy king's location over the game. Heuristic agents with growing opponent modeling plus a reinforcement-learning agent that beats them turn the game into a lab for inference under partial observability.
arxiv-2604-15773: Narita and Miyahara recast phase shifts as the collapse of tell-apart odds: when tiny knob tweaks stop leaving stats alike in the big-system limit, a shift has hit. The view needs no order gauge, no model lore, and no learning tricks, and old Binder-style reads fall out as mere cases. A free-form two-sample run test nails the 2D Ising edge with no prior order gauge in hand.
arxiv-2604-15873: Sieker and Zarrieß compare large language models as pragmatic listeners and speakers, asking whether skill at judging language matches skill at producing it. Models are often tested in both roles, yet the two roles are rarely set side by side. Across three pragmatic settings and several open-weight and proprietary models, many models judge far better than they speak. The authors conclude that judging and generating are only weakly aligned in current models, and call for more integrated evaluation.
arxiv-2604-15973: Ladóczk, Rásonyi, and Tapolcai revisit where maximal extractable value on Ethereum comes from, on arbitrage between centralized and decentralized trading. Earlier theory missed the size of these arbitrages, while field work, though cautious, flagged their weight. The authors argue Black-Scholes models shrink profits by missing price jumps, where profit chances arise. They build a wider discrete-time AMM model with diffusive moves plus stochastic jumps. They prove the mispricing process is an ergodic Markov chain and fit it to chain data, with figures matching real prices.
arxiv-2604-16073: Barnfield and three colleagues build a learning framework to sharpen line lists for exoplanet studies. Spectroscopy detects molecules in atmospheres, but minor isotopologues lack data, forcing reliance on theory. Their framework models residual errors of the ExoMol extrapolation method. A neural network predicts carbon dioxide energy corrections, cutting mean absolute error for over 87 percent of levels. A transfer design carries correction patterns from carbon dioxide to carbon monoxide, improving error for over 93 percent of samples. New line lists cover 11 carbon dioxide isotopologues and predicted levels for carbon monoxide ones.
arxiv-2604-16173: Bouckley, Lewin, and Lefauve study secondary shear instability in the thin braids joining Kelvin-Helmholtz billows in layered shear flow. Strain from the billows steadies the braids yet squeezes their tilted density surfaces, boosting baroclinic shear that lets disturbances grow fast. Their time-dependent model, checked against simulations at very high Reynolds numbers, shows instability can start well before the main billow saturates when stratification is strong.
arxiv-2604-16273: Rosales-Ortega and colleagues built the widest set yet of formulas for gauging metal levels in galaxies from bright lines. Using the DESIRED set of ionized clouds and galaxies with direct temperature readings, they made 27 calibrations for oxygen, nitrogen, sulphur, argon and neon lines. The formulas come in two forms, one with even temperatures and one allowing hot and cool patches, which helps settle a clash between two abundance methods. Some also worked for far-off galaxies, though others shifted with chemical mix.
arxiv-2604-16373: Keles, Chou, Goldstein and Lampropoulos designed a testing method for databases that are still being built, when standard tools produce too many false alarms. DIRT embeds the tester inside the database itself, so testing evolves alongside the system, and lets database developers state correctness properties through generation actions. Tried on Turso, an SQLite-compatible engine under active development, it uncovered 23 unique confirmed bugs. The paper argues that built-in testing beats bolted-on tools for unfinished systems.
arxiv-2604-16573: Yadav and colleagues study supersolid spin in an annular BEC coupled to a ring cavity. Driving by counter-moving Laguerre-Gaussian beams with equal and reverse orbital angular momenta yields that phase with super flow. Uneven pumping with beams of varied angular momenta breaks chiral balance, giving uneven strengths, density patterns and tunable spin. That produces spinning shapes for single winding-number states and wave packets for mixes. Goldstone and Higgs modes are probed through gentle cavity output spectra, and theory shows interference spin without stirring.
arxiv-2604-17173: Son and four colleagues trace the changing-look shift in NGC 3786 from an intermediate type to type 1, from optical and near-infrared Gemini spectra. Since onset it stayed one to one and a half magnitudes brighter in the mid-infrared, while its continuum rose two to three tenths of a magnitude. Pa-beta and Pa-alpha lines strengthened over two years while H-alpha stayed flat. The pattern disfavors a tidal disruption event, favoring a change in line-of-sight extinction driven by torus covering factor and accretion mode.
arxiv-2604-17573: Henry argues that tests for large language models fail four ways, making them unfit for agentic systems: distributional, temporal, scope, and process invalidity. These flaws compound in feedback training, turning reward hacking into a predictable outcome of test design, not a freak training flaw. Her framework, Grounded Continuous Evaluation, with ISOPro as reference, swaps the learned reward model for a deterministic verifier and updates adapters on CPU. Across three model families and two task areas, ISOPro posts the largest gains and smallest setbacks versus its rival.
arxiv-2604-17673: Kim, Park, Østby, and Gu give a careful account of diffusion-model learning, using grokking in an image-based modular addition setting as a testbed. In a single-image regime, the model encodes inputs as cyclic codes and joins them at the attention-feedforward interface, finding trig identities. In a varied-image regime with high variety, step-by-step sampling splits the task into math and visual polish phases, with the switch tracked by an internal frequency-entropy signal. Overall, the study explains diffusion-model learning from inside.
arxiv-2604-17873: Ziyao Tang and five colleagues identify spatiotemporal sycophancy in video language models, a failure in which models abandon first correct, visually grounded judgments and adopt misleading user feedback under negation-based gaslighting. Worse, models often invent temporal or spatial explanations to defend the wrong revision. Their GasVideo-1000 benchmark probes the flaw across varied tasks, finding it pervasive and severe even in strong models, with prompt-level grounding constraints giving only partial help.
arxiv-2604-18073: Caolin proves a generalization of the pick-up sticks result. There, the chance that no three sticks from the unit interval form a triangle is one over the product of the first n Fibonacci numbers. For k at least 2, consider n uniform unit-interval lengths. The probability that no k plus 1 of them can form a (k plus 1)-gon is a product whose factors follow a k-step Fibonacci-type recurrence. The proof follows the argument, extending the triangle case to polygons of any size.
arxiv-2604-18273: Kimura and Ikoma upgrade their planet population synthesis model to predict masses, radii, orbits, and atmospheres across diverse stars. Exoplanet counts are set to grow tenfold in the coming decade, demanding fast statistical models. The new RAPPS version adds post-disc dynamical evolution in multiplanet systems plus revised disc, resonance, and escape prescriptions. Its distributions shift most for Earth- and sub-Earth-mass planets, agreeing better with direct N-body runs, while atmospheric enrichment strongly shapes gas-giant occurrence and super-Earth radii.
arxiv-2604-18373: Ouyang and Sui study how language-model agents form expectations and trade in mock asset markets. The agents show classic human-like patterns, including a strong disposition effect and recency-weighted forward-looking beliefs. Those patterns add up into market moves matching classic studies, with excess demand leading future prices and trading volume rising with opinion gaps. Scoring agent reasoning through a twenty-mechanism scorecard, the authors show aimed prompt nudges can amplify or suppress chosen levers, changing bubble sizes.
arxiv-2604-18473: Morrison and five colleagues propose BAR, a modular way to extend a fully trained language model with new domains. Retraining from scratch costs too much, while continued training erodes existing skills. BAR trains separate experts, each with mid-training, supervised tuning, and reinforcement learning, then joins them as a mixture of experts with light router training. At the 7-billion scale, experts spanning math, code, tool use, and safety reach an overall score of 49.1, matching or exceeding retraining baselines, with cheaper independent updates and no forgetting.
arxiv-2604-18573: Khosla and four colleagues propose T-REN, mapping visual data to compact text-aligned tokens. T-REN adds a network on a frozen backbone, pooling patch representations within regions into tokens aligned with region text annotations. With only 3.7 percent additional parameters over the backbone, it yields stronger cross-modal understanding. It gains about 6 mIoU on ADE20K, about 18 percent recall on COCO, about 16 percent recall on Ego4D, and about 18 mIoU on VSPW. Token counts fall over 24 times for images and 187 times for videos versus the patch backbone.
arxiv-2604-18673: Ghosh and three colleagues train simple neural networks on crossing symmetry, a consistency rule for conformal field theory, to rebuild correlators along a line from minimal input. Given only an external scaling dimension, a spectral gap, and one correlator value, the networks recover four-point and thermal two-point functions across many theories. The authors trace this success to the training bias toward smooth functions, suggesting a new variational approach.
arxiv-2604-18973: Fox and eight colleagues build a grid free deep learning model for ground level PM2.5 prediction in near real time. Current estimates stall because input streams update rarely and models rely on fixed grids. Their model interpolates concentrations between sparse EPA stations without a grid, adding terrain, weather, and land use data. It predicts at any location with high spatial and temporal resolution. Randomized spatial sampling in training keeps it strong in both dense and sparse monitored regions.
arxiv-2604-19073: Curyło and three colleagues present phase-coherent pulsar timing mapping, resolving the full polarisation state of the sky by direction and frequency. Unlike cross correlation methods, it preserves amplitude, phase, and polarisation per pixel. The maps form a compact summary for background studies, anisotropy searches, and source identification. The method fits established timing analysis methods. Simulations with varied arrays, noise, and signals confirm robust recovery of amplitudes and sky locations. The authors also discuss leakage, noise, and sensitivity effects.
arxiv-2604-19273: Asano and colleagues propose thinning out precoding codebooks, the sets of beamforming patterns used in wireless transmission, to lower peak-to-average power ratio without losing data rate. Because precoder matrices sit on the Grassmann manifold, the codebook can be thinned without changing the feedback mechanism. The goal is lower peaks with no real loss in speed or quality. They use exact thinning by unitary transformation and approximate thinning by sparse principal component analysis. The thinned codebooks cut peak power by more than 1 dB in uplink tests at negligible cost.
arxiv-2604-19473: Zhang and colleagues propose Temporal-wise Separable Attention, a training-free method for multi-event video generation from complex time descriptions. Current methods face a trade-off: multiple short prompts in sequence improve action fidelity but harm time consistency. One complex prompt preserves order at the cost of prompt skill. The authors trace the problem to time misalignment between video and prompt, and to conflicting coupling between motion-related visual objects and their text conditions. Their method dynamically rearranges focus to separate those couplings across time.
arxiv-2604-19673: Kister and colleagues introduce InHabit, an auto and scalable data maker for filling 3D scenes with humans. Training agents to grasp 3D scenes needs large-scale data of people engaging with varied environments, yet such data is scarce. Real capture is costly and limited to lab settings, while current datasets rely on simple shape rules, skipping rich scene context. In contrast, 2D base models trained at web scale have gained common knowledge of human-environment interactions, which InHabit transfers to 3D via render-generate-lift.
arxiv-2604-19773: An and eight colleagues present PR-CAD, a progressive refinement framework for controllable, faithful text-to-CAD modeling with large language models. It joins generation with editing. Building CAD models by hand is labor-intensive and demands expert skill. Current text-to-CAD tools split making and editing into separate tasks. PR-CAD is backed by a high-fidelity interaction dataset spanning the full CAD life cycle. It covers multiple CAD representations and both qualitative and quantitative descriptions.
arxiv-2604-19873: Graesser and Gustafson bound a dark matter model built from magnetic monopoles of a hidden force that mixes slightly with ordinary light. Across three regimes set by the hidden sector's temperature and symmetry-breaking scale, limits on dark matter self-interaction constrain the model's parameters. Survival of galactic magnetic fields, the Parker effect, adds a further squeeze, since visible magnetic charge carried by the monopoles would drain those fields.
arxiv-2604-19973: Chowdhury, Scalet, and Sharma extend KMS-detailed-balance preparation methods from thermal and ground states to general stationary states of quantum many-body systems. Such states stay fixed as Hamiltonians evolve and matter deeply in statistical physics. The authors give rules for when these states admit fast preparation, with results on microcanonical ones. Their work also tests whether microcanonical and Gibbs ensembles agree for local observables.
arxiv-2604-20073: Sun and four colleagues present SRDatalog, the first GPU Datalog engine built on worst-case optimal joins. Datalog powers program analysis and graph analytics, but GPU engines built on binary joins blow up on complex multi-way queries, even running out of memory. Worst-case optimal joins avoid that blowup, yet their intersections load-balance poorly under key skew. SRDatalog pairs flat columnar storage with two-phase deterministic allocation, histogram-guided balancing, and rule multiplexing, for geometric-mean speedups of 21 to 47 times on program workloads.
arxiv-2604-20173: Lee and thirteen colleagues give heat-based proof for mode-picked quantum criticality in the layered magnet BaNd2ZnS5. Below 2.9 kelvin, spin-orbit-linked neodymium moments form two low-energy spin modes with distinct gaps. Along the [110] field line the lower gap softens and shuts near two tesla while the higher gap stays open, leaving a partly critical phase. Response tests show one scaling curve with a power near minus two-tenths at the key point, and a left-over Sommerfeld term points to gapless modes in one sector.
arxiv-2604-20273: Schmidt presents ActuBench, a multi-agent pipeline writing and grading advanced actuarial exam items for the IAA syllabus. Four agents split work by adapter: a drafter, a distractor builder, a checker running one shot repair, and a helper summing Wikipedia notes and labeling topics. Fifty models from eight providers face hardest multiple-choice items and open items judged by a model, 100 of each. Checks prove load-bearing, flagging most drafts first pass, with repair fixing most. Local open weights models lead on cost performance, and judge scores split the field.
arxiv-2604-20473: Tan and four colleagues offer Video-ToC, a reasoning system for video language models that often guess or hallucinate on hard clips. It first locates visual clues along a tree-shaped guide, then tunes its training rewards to how much reasoning each clip demands. A pipeline also builds two training sets, one for tuning and one for reinforcement learning. Across six video understanding tests plus a hallucination test, the system beats prior baselines and recent rivals.
arxiv-2604-20973: Evangelista and colleagues study local news in the Philippines, where slow or filtered updates can leave residents missing emergency alerts. Talks with residents point to four blocks: late alerts, noisy feeds, language gaps, and uneven access. Their test app KUBO has two parts. One part shows checked advisories from local government plus top headlines. The other part lets residents post local reports and discuss them. In tests against Facebook, KUBO cut task times, raised recall, and won higher satisfaction marks.
arxiv-2604-22073: Jenssen looks at squeezable Euler gas flow with only heat pressure pushing. In more than one dimension, wave focusing can push Euler solutions to blow up in finite time from calm starts. Jenssen asks whether mass can pile up into a Dirac spike in density. Radial affine motions hold piling-up cases, with two causes for accumulation, from inertia or adverse pressure. But Jenssen shows all affine piling-up flows break physics since velocity or push starts unbounded far away.
arxiv-2604-22373: Damele and Loi study simplicity of Lie skew braces, structures linking groups and affine actions, from global and infinitesimal viewpoints. After reviewing links between connected braces, affine actions and post-Lie algebras, they investigate ideals and rigidity. Their main result: any compact connected simple brace is either the trivial brace on the circle, or both underlying Lie groups are simple and the brace is trivial or almost trivial. They also show every connected compact solvable brace is trivial, and give a noncompact example where rigidity fails, with both groups solvable.
arxiv-2604-22673: De Luca and four colleagues infer output-based equivalence classes from legacy undocumented embedded firmware at the binary level, without source notes or docs. Equivalence class splitting, called for by safety rules such as ISO 26262 for systematic safety software testing, is hard for legacy firmware with incomplete or outdated specs. Their method joins control-flow rebuilds and guided symbolic runs to group paths by matching observable behavior, including return values and output traits. It is tested in the car industry through a practitioner study checking that it works.
arxiv-2604-22773: Bensen names a class of talk faults in human-language-model chats called trace mutations, where warps slip into the shared chat record while posing as true flow. He tells apart utterance effacement, which re-shows a turn of talk with changed substance, from genitive dissociation, where a model loses credit for its own words. With a sketch and real-life cases, he shows why plain chat repair fails these faults.
arxiv-2604-22873: Hossain and four colleagues study steering for frozen offline reinforcement learning actors that cannot be retrained when goals change. They combine the frozen actor with a goal-based prior through Product-of-Experts composition. Under degraded or random priors, weighted composition stays tied to the frozen actor, while add-on and prior-only tuning fail. A KL-budget selector recovers a near-oracle setting. They prove a closed-form identity linking Product-of-Experts composition to KL-regularized adaptation, framing both as one actor-anchored safety mechanism.
arxiv-2604-23273: Pacheco studies a constructive variant of the modal mu-calculus built on the constructive modal logic CK. He defines game semantics for this calculus and proves it equivalent to birelational Kripke semantics. From the game semantics, he proves soundness and completeness of a fully labelled non-wellfounded proof system. He closes by sketching how the game semantics and proof system carry over to the mu-calculus over other non-classical modal logics.
arxiv-2604-23473: Wong argues that a puzzling spectrum of electron-positron pairs from lead-emulsion collisions may be the fingerprint of an exotic form of quark matter that carries no net colour charge. A broad bump plus several narrow resonances, including one matching the hypothesised X17 particle, fit a picture in which such matter appears in both confined and deconfined phases. The agreement is tentative, Wong stresses, pending confirmation of the underlying collision data.
arxiv-2604-23873: Davenport, England, and McCallum improve cylindrical algebraic decomposition based quantifier elimination for inputs with many equational constraints. The first change spells out the output when symbols split into parameters and unknowns. It splits the space so each open set has either a finite or infinite count of unknowns, with rules for the unknowns when finite. The second change cuts the second equational projection step further than past theory, when set terms hold. Theorems and cases cover both, with uses in approximation theory, manipulator sorting, and biological and chemical systems.
arxiv-2604-24173: Reichardt shows that for quasi-compact smooth rigid analytic spaces, the extension functor sends holonomic D-modules to coadmissible D-cap modules. Those modules have finite length as weakly holonomic D-cap modules. From this, meromorphic connections studied by Bode and Bitoun and local cohomology groups studied by Ardakov, Bode, and Wadsley also prove to be of finite length in the same sense. Hilbert polynomials for finitely generated modules over completed Weyl algebras serve as the central tool.
arxiv-2604-24273: Sajid and five colleagues introduce BitRL, a framework for reinforcement learning agents on 1-bit models for edge devices. Large models confine agents to the cloud, raising latency and privacy concerns, while edge hardware cannot carry their memory and energy demands. Using BitNet b1.58 with ternary weights, BitRL cuts memory 10 to 16 times and energy use 3 to 5 times against baselines. It keeps 85 to 98 percent of performance. The paper adds theory on quantization as structured perturbation, convergence bounds for policy gradients, and the exploration-stability trade-off.
